ProtT5 Phosphorylation Prediction — Interpretation Report

Source: ProtT5_phosphorylation_clean_pipeline.ipynb  |  Embeddings: ProtT5-XL-UniRef50 • 1024-dim  |  Task: binary protein-level phosphorylation classification

1. Dataset

Proteins from the manually curated UniProt/Swiss-Prot human proteome were split into two mutually exclusive classes using the Post-translational modification free-text field:

  • Positive (phosphorylated): entry text contains “phospho” or “phosphorylation”
  • Negative (not phosphorylated): no match to the above pattern

Duplicate protein names were removed within each class and any overlap between classes was discarded. This labelling procedure is identical to the Ankh and ESM2 pipelines, enabling fair cross-model comparisons.

Figure 1. Class distribution. Phosphorylated proteins represent 14.2% of the dataset.

Class imbalance note: With only 14.2% positive examples, PR-AUC (Average Precision) is the primary metric throughout. A random classifier would achieve PR-AUC ≈ 0.142. Models are trained with explicit imbalance corrections (balanced class weights for logistic regression; BCEWithLogitsLoss pos_weight = neg/pos for MLP).

2. Methods

2.1 Embeddings

ProtT5-XL-UniRef50 (Elnaggar et al., 2021) protein language model embeddings (1024-dimensional) were loaded from a pre-built cache. ProtT5 is a T5-based encoder-decoder trained on UniRef50 sequences with a span-corruption objective. Two global sequence representations were evaluated:

  • Max pooling — element-wise maximum across the residue dimension
  • Attention pooling — learned weighted average across residues

All features were z-score normalised (StandardScaler) using training-set statistics only to prevent data leakage. The 1024-dim ProtT5 vectors sit between Ankh (768-dim) and ESM-2 (1280-dim) in size.

2.2 Classifiers

All experiments use an 80/20 stratified train/test split (seed 42).

5. Interpretation

5.1 Primary Metric: PR-AUC

Because phosphorylated proteins comprise only 14.2% of the dataset, PR-AUC is the principal evaluation criterion. ROC-AUC can be misleadingly optimistic in highly imbalanced settings. The random PR-AUC baseline is 0.142; values well above this confirm model utility.

5.2 MLP vs Logistic Regression

MLP (attn pooling) PR-AUC: 0.4436  |  MLP (max pooling) PR-AUC: 0.4543
LR (attn pooling) PR-AUC: 0.3937  |  LR (max pooling) PR-AUC: 0.4124

Both architectures benefit from class-imbalance correction. The non-linear MLP generally improves PR-AUC over logistic regression when the embedding space is not linearly separable.

5.3 Max Pool vs Attention Pool

Attention pooling uses a learned per-residue weighting and tends to retain biologically relevant positional information, whereas max pooling retains peak activations. The PR-AUC delta between the two pooling strategies reflects this difference.

5.4 Cross-Model Context

ProtT5-XL uses 1024-dimensional embeddings, between Ankh (768-dim) and ESM-2 (1280-dim). Dimensionality alone does not determine quality; model architecture, training corpus, and pre-training objective all contribute. Comparing results_phosphorylation_ProtT5/, results_phosphorylation_ESM2/, and results_phosphorylation/ (Ankh) provides a direct three-way model comparison on identical data and train/test splits.

5.5 UMAP vs PCA / t-SNE

UMAP (Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection) is included alongside PCA and t-SNE because it better preserves global structure at larger scales. Convergence (or divergence) across all three projections strengthens confidence in the visual interpretation of embedding separability.

5.6 Recommendations for Future Work

  1. Residue-level classifier: Train a per-token binary classifier on ProtT5 token embeddings to predict phosphorylatable Ser/Thr/Tyr residues directly.
  2. Structured labelling: Extract exact phosphosite positions from the UniProt Modified residue column for cleaner, position-specific labels.
  3. Cross-validation: Replace single 80/20 split with 5-fold stratified CV
  4. Feature combination: Concatenate max-pool and attention-pool vectors (2×1024-dim) to capture complementary representations.
  5. Fine-tuning: Fine-tune ProtT5 end-to-end rather than using frozen embeddings.
  6. Ensemble: Combine ProtT5, ESM2 and Ankh embeddings for a richer feature set.
